But then, a mean boy comes to the fountain. He has a bucket in his hand. He fills the bucket with water and pours it on Anna. Anna gets wet and cold. She stops dancing and starts to cry.

"Ha ha, you're not a dancer, you're a wet rat!" the boy laughs.

"Hey, stop that! That's not nice!" Anna's mom says. She runs to Anna and hugs her. Anna's dad goes to the boy and takes his bucket away.

"Apologize to Anna right now. You don't pour water on people. That's rude and mean." Anna's dad says.

The boy looks scared and sorry. He says sorry to Anna. Anna's mom gives her a towel and a hug. She says it's okay, she's still a dancer and a princess.

Anna feels better. She smiles and says thank you. She decides to forgive the boy. She asks him if he wants to dance with her. The boy nods and says yes. They dance around the fountain together. They have fun and make friends. Anna's mom and dad watch them and smile. They are proud of Anna. She is a kind and brave dancer.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Gemma. She liked to draw pictures and was very good at it. One day, Gemma's mom demanded that she take a picture of the park.

Gemma grabbed her art supplies and went to the park. It was very noisy. There were kids playing and people talking. Gemma quickly set up her easel and grabbed her colored pencils. She then began to draw the scene around her.

She worked hard and created the best picture she had ever drawn. Gemma was so pleased with her drawing that she ran back home to show her mom.

When Gemma showed her mom the picture, she was delighted. She gave Gemma a big hug and praised her. From then on, Gemma was always ready to demand better when it came to her artwork.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their dolls. They liked to pretend they were doctors and nurses, and they had a small bag with bandages and stickers. They carried their dolls to a bench and put them on a blanket.

"Your doll is very sick," Anna said to Ben. "She needs a serious operation."

Ben nodded. He was worried about his doll. He hoped Anna could make her better. He watched as Anna took out a bandage and wrapped it around the doll's head.

"Good job, doctor," Ben said. "But what about her leg? It looks broken."

Anna frowned. She did not have any more bandages. She looked around and saw a sign on a fence. It said "Do not enter. Construction site. Danger."

Anna had an idea. She said to Ben, "I know where we can find more bandages. Come with me."

She grabbed her doll and ran to the fence. She did not see the big word "no" on the sign. She did not know what it meant. She thought it was part of the fence. She lifted the fence and crawled under it. Ben followed her.

They saw a big pile of wood and metal. They looked like bandages to them. They carried some of them to their dolls. They did not hear the loud noise of a truck coming closer.

The truck driver saw the fence was open. He was angry. He said, "Hey, you kids! What are you doing here? This is a law. You cannot be here. It is very dangerous. Get out now!"

Anna and Ben were scared. They dropped the wood and metal and ran back to the fence. They did not want to get in trouble. They did not want to get hurt. They carried their dolls and their bag and ran to their mom.

Their mom was waiting for them on a bench. She saw their faces and their dolls. She said, "What happened? Why are your dolls so dirty? And what are those things on their heads and legs?"

Anna and Ben told her what they did. They said they were sorry. They did not know it was a law. They did not know it was dangerous. They just wanted to help their dolls.

Their mom hugged them. She said, "I'm glad you are safe. But you have to be careful. You have to listen to the signs. They are there for a reason. They tell you what you can and cannot do. They are serious. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They said they understood. They said they would not do it again. They said they loved their mom. Their mom smiled. She said she loved them too. She said they could go home and clean their dolls. She said they could play doctor and nurse again. But only with bandages and stickers.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and going outside to play in the sun. One day, Lily's mom asked her to deliver a package to their neighbor.

Lily was so excited to help her mom. She grabbed the package and ran outside. The package was wrapped in brown leather and she held it tightly in her little hands.

As she walked to the neighbor's house, she saw some kids playing with a ball. They asked her to play with them, but she said she couldn't because she had to deliver the package.

When she arrived at the neighbor's house, she knocked on the door. The neighbor opened the door and said, "Thank you for delivering this package, Lily. You are such a good helper." Lily felt proud and happy, not ashamed like she had felt earlier when she couldn't play with the other kids.

Once upon a time there was a lady who wanted to give a special gift. She thought and thought about what to give and finally came up with an idea.

The lady went to a shop and bought some blocks and pieces. She brought them home and put them together to make a structure. Everyone was amazed at how tall it was! It was so big that it almost touched the sky!

The lady loved the structure very much, but one day something bad happened; someone rude came along and destroyed the structure. The lady was very sad and almost cried.

But then, something wonderful happened. All the people around her came together and helped her build the structure again. They put all the blocks and pieces together and soon it was back in its original state.

The lady was so very happy! She thanked everyone for their help, understanding how important it was to her.

From that day forward, the lady was very careful to make sure nothing bad ever happened to the structure again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She liked to wear her favorite dress with flowers on it. One day, she went to the kitchen and saw her mom setting the table. The table had a red cloth on it and ordinary plates.

Lily asked her mom if she could help set the table. Her mom said yes, so Lily put the forks and spoons on the table. Then, she saw her dad coming home from work. He was wearing his ordinary suit.

Lily was happy to see her dad and they all sat down to eat dinner together at the table. It was a nice night for Lily and her family.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was looking for something to pick. He saw a jet in the deep sky. The little boy wanted to pick the jet. He felt so happy.

He jumped up and grabbed the jet. He started to fly around in the sky. The little boy was so excited. He made big deep circles in the sky.

Suddenly, the little boy heard a loud noise. He looked down and saw a big truck. The truck was so big and strong. The truck had to pick up the jet.

The little boy was sad that he had to let go of the jet. He waved goodbye as the truck drove away with the jet in the back. The little boy watched until he couldn't see the jet anymore.

The little boy was sad, but he knew the jet would be happy with the truck. He smiled and went back home. He had a wonderful time and would never forget it!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a red box. Inside the red box was a pair of scissors. She liked the scissors a lot. Every day, she would take them outside and sit in the grass and play with them.

The scissors grew very big in the grass. Soon they were bigger than the red box. Every day, the scissors grew and grew until they were big enough to use to cut the grass.

The little girl had so much fun playing with the scissors and cutting the grass. She liked the feeling of being tough and strong, like grown-ups.

The little girl learned a valuable lesson - when you work hard and grow, you can do amazing things.

Once there was a big tree. Everyday it grew and grew. One day, a silly bird hopped onto the tree. The bird was looking for something shiny to wear.

The bird said, "I'm looking for something to make me look fancy!" She added, "Do you know where I can find something glimmering?"

The tree thought for a moment and then said, "Yes, follow me! I can help you find it."

The bird followed the tree and soon they found a sparkling spell on the ground. The bird cheered and said, "This is perfect! Now I'm the prettiest bird around!"

The bird thanked the tree and flew away. The tree just smiled and kept growing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play at the shore, where the water meets the sand. One day, she saw a silly crab walking along the shore. The crab was moving sideways and Lily thought it looked funny.

Suddenly, Lily's little brother came running towards her. He was crying because he lost his favorite toy. Lily knew how much the toy meant to her brother, so she started to look for it. She searched high and low, until she found it buried in the sand. Her brother was so happy and gave her a big hug. Lily felt proud and happy that she could help her brother.

From that day on, every time Lily went to the shore, she kept an eye out for her brother's toy. She knew how much it meant to him and she wanted to make sure it was always safe. And sometimes, when she was lucky, she would see the silly crab again, moving sideways along the shore.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. One day, he went to the park to play with his friend, Sammy. They were having a great time until Timmy's favorite toy car got stuck in the mud. He tried to pull it out, but it wouldn't budge.

Sammy said, "Let's ask the big kids for help!"

Timmy replied, "No, they always make fun of me because I'm little."

Sammy said, "Don't worry, I'll go ask them for you."

Sammy went over to the big kids and said, "Can you help my friend Timmy? His toy car is stuck in the mud."

The big kids said, "Sure, we'll help him."

Timmy was surprised and happy that the big kids helped him. He surrendered his toy car to them and they pulled it out of the mud. Timmy thanked them and they all played together. The gloomy feeling Timmy had before was gone and he had a great day with his friends.

Once upon a time in a land far away, there lived a young girl. Her name was Sarah and everyday she would wake up in her beautiful bedroom. She would look out the window and see bright birds, green trees and blue sky. One morning, Sarah woke up and decided she wanted to explore the world.

So, she put on her shoes and went outside. As she walked, she saw different things like tall buildings, little animals and nice people. She said hi to them all and waved.

She came to a big field with a river through the middle of it. Sarah lay down and looked up. The sky was so blue and the clouds so white. She saw them move and change shapes.

Suddenly she noticed a little baby rabbit near her. Sarah smiled and the rabbit hopped away. She followed the baby rabbit and saw something even more beautiful. A big garden of many colours - green, pink, yellow, orange and purple.

The young girl was in awe and said, "This place is so beautiful". She spent the rest of the day playing and discovering the world around her. At night, she went back home, dreaming of all the beautiful things she'd seen.

Once there were two bears, Bob and Sue. They both wanted to race to see who was the fastest, but Bob decided to ignore Sue's suggestion.

Bob thought he could easily win the race, but he was wrong. Sue had been very fast and modest, and she won the race by a lot!

Bob was very angry about Sue's victory, so he ignored her again! But Sue didn't think it was fair, so she yelled until Bob was forced to look at her.

Finally Bob realized that Sue was the victor and he complimented her on her modest racing skills. From that day on, they were always very nice to each other and shared many wonderful races!

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Jack. He was bright orange and had stripes all over his body. Jack wanted to be the best swimmer in the ocean!

Every day, Jack practiced hard and would dive really deep into the ocean. When Jack stopped to eat his meal, he would see all the other fish swimming around and think to himself that he wanted to be just like them.

One day, Jack was feeling really proud about his diving skills. So proud, that he decided to challenge all the other fish in the ocean. Jack said he could dive deeper than any of the other fish!

At first, all the other fish laughed at Jack and said his dive would be impossible. But, Jack refused to give up. He took a deep breath, held it in and dove down to the deepest depths of the ocean.

The other fish gasped with surprise when Jack managed to make it to the depths of the ocean! They were so proud of Jack and could not believe that he had accomplished such an amazing feat.

Jack learned a valuable lesson that day. He learned that with determination and hard work, you can achieve anything!

One day, a little girl found something perfect in the ground. It was a shiny, silver tap. She was so happy and couldn't believe her luck. She wanted to keep it, so she took a big spoon and dug a hole in the ground. She put the tap inside and then filled the hole back up. She called it "burying the tap".

The little girl was very proud of herself. She had buried the tap all by herself, and it was so perfect. She had kept it safe and nobody else could have it. She ran back home to tell her mommy and daddy all about it.

The next day, the girl went back to the spot where she had buried the tap. To her surprise, the tap was gone. Where could it have gone? She looked and looked but couldn't find it anywhere. She was very sad, but then realized that this was part of the game of burying the tap. She was glad that she had buried it so that it could find a new home.

Once there were two twins, Jack and Jill. Jack was very rude, always pushing Jill and grabbing the toys from her. Today, the two were playing in their playroom and Jill was getting very frustrated. She asked Jack, "Why are you so rude?"

Jack answered, "Because I want to win!"

Jill replied, "But why? Winning doesn't mean you have to be rude!"

Jack thought for a minute and then said, "I'm sorry. I won't be rude anymore."

Jill smiled and hugged her twin, happy that he had given her an answer. They went back to playing together and had a great time!

Lily and Ben were very excited. It was almost Christmas and they wanted to decorate their house. They had a big box of shiny things and a green tree in the living room.

"Can I put this star on the top of the tree?" Lily asked, holding a yellow star.

"Yes, you can. But be careful, the tree is tall. I will help you," Ben said, lifting his sister up.

They put the star on the tree and then added more shiny things. They had red balls, silver bells, and colorful lights. The tree looked very pretty.

"Now we need to decorate the chimney," Ben said, pointing to the old chimney in the corner. "Maybe Santa will come and bring us presents."

"Okay, let's do it," Lily said, grabbing a long sock. "I will hang this sock on the chimney. Maybe Santa will fill it with candy."

They hung their socks on the chimney and then added some more shiny things. They had paper chains, glittery snowflakes, and a picture of Santa. The chimney looked very festive.

"Wow, we did a good job," Ben said, admiring their work.

"Yes, we did. I hope Santa likes it too," Lily said, smiling.

They hugged each other and then ran to their mom, who was baking cookies in the kitchen.

"Mom, mom, look what we did!" they shouted, pulling her to the living room.

Mom looked at the tree and the chimney and smiled.

"You did a wonderful job, my sweeties. You are very creative and thoughtful. I'm sure Santa will love it too," she said, kissing them on their cheeks.

They all sat on the couch and ate some cookies, feeling happy and proud. They couldn't wait for Christmas morning.

Robbie was a very proud little three year old boy. He loved playing outside and running around the garden with his friends.

One day, Robbie was outside and he suddenly had the urge to run to the bathroom. Without a second thought, he raced inside and ran straight to the bathroom.

He felt so proud of himself for running to the bathroom all by himself without any help. He made it there just in time, too!

Afterwards, Robbie washed his hands, said his thankful prayers and ran back outside to play with his friends. He felt so proud that he had been able to run and make it to the bathroom all by himself.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He was very creative. He wanted to have an adventure. One day he had an idea. He let himself escape from his house. It was fun!

He ran and ran until he got to the park. He climbed up a tree and discovered an amazing view. He saw lots of animals and even a lake. It was magical!

The boy stayed in the park for the whole day. It was his secret place. He let his imagination go wild and had lots of fun.

In the evening, the boy went back home. He had made a creative escape and had the most exciting day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go on picnics with her family. One day, her mommy asked her to help pack the picnic basket. Lily was so helpful and put in sandwiches, fruit, and cookies.

When they got to the park, Lily's daddy took out a tape measure to see how big the picnic blanket was. Lily thought it was funny and wanted to measure things too. She measured how tall the trees were and how long the slide was.

After they ate their yummy picnic, Lily's mommy asked her to help clean up. Lily was happy to help and threw away the trash. She felt proud of herself for being so helpful. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a hero. He had a special job - he had to store all the smooth rocks, so no one could take them away. He was a very special hero!

Every day, the hero would climb up a big hill and store the smooth rocks. He knew it was very important work and he was proud of himself!

At the end of the day, the hero would head back down the hill with bags full of smooth rocks. He was exhausted but happy. He knew he'd done a great job, and he'd help to keep the rocks safe.

And that's what the hero did every single day. On and on, he'd gather and store smooth rocks - and he was the bravest hero ever.

Once upon a time, there was a fox. He was a brave fox and he liked to skip. One day, the fox decided to explore a big, old castle.

As he stepped inside, the fox heard a loud noise. It was coming from the chamber. He tiptoed closer to look inside. It was dark and dull inside the chamber.

The fox saw a big, scary monster. It had large, wiggly arms and was making a loud rumbling sound. The fox was scared but he was brave. He held his breath and quietly tiptoed away.

Suddenly, the monster noticed the fox. He jumped up and started to chase him. The fox quickly ran away and started to skip. He skipped faster than he ever had before, trying to get away from the monster. Finally, the fox made it out of the castle and was safe.

Mama had made some delicious pies. She asked Tim to help her get them out of the oven. Tim was only three years old, but he was very eager and excited to help.

He carefully lifted the pies out and put them on the counter. Mama said, "They look delicious - Why don't you eat one, Tim!" Tim happily agreed and he ate the pie in no time.

Just then, they heard the doorbell ringing. Mama opened the door and a little girl from the neighbourhood was standing outside.

Mama said, "Hi there! Come on in."

The little girl said, "Hi, I thought I heard Tim singing. Could we play together?"

Mama said, "Yes of course! He's been so restless all day; playing will be good for him."

So, the two little kids played together for the rest of the day. They laughed and laughed, and had so much fun playing together. Mama was happy to see them having a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a playful dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play with his friends. One day, Spot saw a new player in the park. The player was a little boy named Tim.

Spot wanted to invite Tim to play with him, so he ran up to Tim and said, "Hi, I am Spot. Do you want to play with me?" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, I want to play with you, Spot!"

They played all day in the park. They ran, jumped, and laughed together. Spot and Tim became best friends. And from that day on, they played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived on a ranch with her mommy and daddy. Lily loved to play outside and explore the big fields.

One day, Lily went to school and wore her favorite black dress. But when she got to school, she realized that her dress had a big stain on it. She felt embarrassed in front of her friends.

After school, Lily went back to the ranch and told her mommy what happened. Her mommy gave her a big hug and said, "Don't worry, Lily. It's okay to make mistakes. We all have accidents sometimes." Lily felt better and went back to playing in the fields, happy to be home where she felt safe and loved.

Sandy was a kind 3 year old girl. One day, she was in her bedroom playing. She wanted to make a surprise for her mom and dad. Sandy had an idea! She took off her pants and filled them with stuffing from her old pillow. After she was done, she put the pants on the floor. Then she clapped her hands and said 'rise!' Suddenly, the stuffed pants rose up. Sandy clapped and laughed. She knew that mom and dad would love her surprise. Sandy gave the stuffed pants a big hug. She was so happy that her special surprise was finished.

Now, Sandy could show her parents her special surprise. She ran into the living room and said "Look mom and dad, I made something special". Mom and dad admired Sandy's surprise. They were so proud of her. Sandy smiled, she knew that she had made something special with her kind heart.

Lily and Ben were playing hide and seek in the park. Lily was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Lily counted to ten and then looked for Ben. She saw a big tree with a hole in it. She thought Ben might be hiding there.

She ran to the tree and peeked inside the hole. It was very dark and she could not see anything. She heard a small voice say, "Boo!"

Lily jumped back and screamed. She saw Ben come out of the hole, laughing. He had a flashlight in his hand.

"Ben, you scared me!" Lily said. "Why did you hide in the dark hole?"

Ben smiled and said, "I wanted to find a good hiding spot. The dark hole was perfect. No one can see me there."

Lily frowned and said, "But it is not fun to hide in the dark. It is scary and cold. And you can't see anything."

Ben shrugged and said, "I don't mind the dark. I have my flashlight. And I can see you when you come close."

Lily shook her head and said, "I don't like the dark. It makes me feel alone and sad. And I can't see your face."

Ben looked at Lily and saw that she was upset. He felt sorry for scaring her. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to make you feel bad. Do you want me to explain why I like the dark?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. Explain to me why you like the dark."

Ben took Lily's hand and said, "Come, I'll show you." He led her to the hole and turned on his flashlight. He said, "Look, the dark is not so bad. It is like a secret place where you can imagine anything. You can pretend you are in a cave, or a spaceship, or a castle. You can make up stories and have fun."

Lily looked at the hole and saw that it was not so scary with the flashlight. She saw some rocks, some leaves, and some bugs. She said, "I see. The dark is like a game. You can use your flashlight to make shapes and shadows."

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, exactly. The dark is like a game. And you can play with me. We can be friends in the dark."

Lily smiled and said, "OK, Ben. I'll try to play with you in the dark. But can we also play in the light sometimes?"

Ben smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. We can play in the light too. We can play hide and seek anywhere. As long as we are together."

Lily hugged Ben and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. You explained to me why you like the dark. And you made me feel better."

Ben hugged Lily and said, "You're welcome, Lily. You are a good friend too. You listened to me and you gave me a chance. And you made me happy."

They both laughed and said, "Let's play again!"

They ran out of the hole and looked for a new hiding spot. They played until it was time to go home. They had fun in the dark and in the light. They were happy.

THE KING OF THE GOLDEN MOUNTAIN

There was once a merchant who had only one child, a son, that was very

young, and barely able to run alone. He had two richly laden ships then

making a voyage upon the seas, in which he had embarked all his wealth,

in the hope of making great gains, when the news came that both were

lost. Thus from being a rich man he became all at once so very poor that

nothing was left to him but one small plot of land; and there he often

went in an evening to take his walk, and ease his mind of a little of

his trouble.

One day, as he was roaming along in a brown study, thinking with no

great comfort on what he had been and what he now was, and was like

to be, all on a sudden there stood before him a little, rough-looking,

black dwarf. 'Prithee, friend, why so sorrowful?' said he to the

merchant; 'what is it you take so deeply to heart?' 'If you would do me

any good I would willingly tell you,' said the merchant. 'Who knows but

I may?' said the little man: 'tell me what ails you, and perhaps you

will find I may be of some use.' Then the merchant told him how all his

wealth was gone to the bottom of the sea, and how he had nothing left

but that little plot of land. 'Oh, trouble not yourself about that,'

said the dwarf; 'only undertake to bring me here, twelve years hence,

whatever meets you first on your going home, and I will give you as much

as you please.' The merchant thought this was no great thing to ask;

that it would most likely be his dog or his cat, or something of that

sort, but forgot his little boy Heinel; so he agreed to the bargain, and

signed and sealed the bond to do what was asked of him.

But as he drew near home, his little boy was so glad to see him that he

crept behind him, and laid fast hold of his legs, and looked up in

his face and laughed. Then the father started, trembling with fear and

horror, and saw what it was that he had bound himself to do; but as no

gold was come, he made himself easy by thinking that it was only a joke

that the dwarf was playing him, and that, at any rate, when the money

came, he should see the bearer, and would not take it in.

About a month afterwards he went upstairs into a lumber-room to look

for some old iron, that he might sell it and raise a little money; and

there, instead of his iron, he saw a large pile of gold lying on the

floor. At the sight of this he was overjoyed, and forgetting all about

his son, went into trade again, and became a richer merchant than

before.

Meantime little Heinel grew up, and as the end of the twelve years drew

near the merchant began to call to mind his bond, and became very sad

and thoughtful; so that care and sorrow were written upon his face. The

boy one day asked what was the matter, but his father would not tell for

some time; at last, however, he said that he had, without knowing it,

sold him for gold to a little, ugly-looking, black dwarf, and that the

twelve years were coming round when he must keep his word. Then Heinel

said, 'Father, give yourself very little trouble about that; I shall be

too much for the little man.'

When the time came, the father and son went out together to the place

agreed upon: and the son drew a circle on the ground, and set himself

and his father in the middle of it. The little black dwarf soon came,

and walked round and round about the circle, but could not find any way

to get into it, and he either could not, or dared not, jump over it. At

last the boy said to him. 'Have you anything to say to us, my friend, or

what do you want?' Now Heinel had found a friend in a good fairy, that

was fond of him, and had told him what to do; for this fairy knew what

good luck was in store for him. 'Have you brought me what you said you

would?' said the dwarf to the merchant. The old man held his tongue, but

Heinel said again, 'What do you want here?' The dwarf said, 'I come to

talk with your father, not with you.' 'You have cheated and taken in my

father,' said the son; 'pray give him up his bond at once.' 'Fair and

softly,' said the little old man; 'right is right; I have paid my money,

and your father has had it, and spent it; so be so good as to let me

have what I paid it for.' 'You must have my consent to that first,' said

Heinel, 'so please to step in here, and let us talk it over.' The old

man grinned, and showed his teeth, as if he should have been very glad

to get into the circle if he could. Then at last, after a long talk,

they came to terms. Heinel agreed that his father must give him up, and

that so far the dwarf should have his way: but, on the other hand, the

fairy had told Heinel what fortune was in store for him, if he followed

his own course; and he did not choose to be given up to his hump-backed

friend, who seemed so anxious for his company.

So, to make a sort of drawn battle of the matter, it was settled that

Heinel should be put into an open boat, that lay on the sea-shore hard

by; that the father should push him off with his own hand, and that he

should thus be set adrift, and left to the bad or good luck of wind and

weather. Then he took leave of his father, and set himself in the boat,

but before it got far off a wave struck it, and it fell with one side

low in the water, so the merchant thought that poor Heinel was lost, and

went home very sorrowful, while the dwarf went his way, thinking that at

any rate he had had his revenge.

The boat, however, did not sink, for the good fairy took care of her

friend, and soon raised the boat up again, and it went safely on. The

young man sat safe within, till at length it ran ashore upon an unknown

land. As he jumped upon the shore he saw before him a beautiful castle

but empty and dreary within, for it was enchanted. 'Here,' said he to

himself, 'must I find the prize the good fairy told me of.' So he once

more searched the whole palace through, till at last he found a white

snake, lying coiled up on a cushion in one of the chambers.

Now the white snake was an enchanted princess; and she was very glad

to see him, and said, 'Are you at last come to set me free? Twelve

long years have I waited here for the fairy to bring you hither as she

promised, for you alone can save me. This night twelve men will come:

their faces will be black, and they will be dressed in chain armour.

They will ask what you do here, but give no answer; and let them do

what they will--beat, whip, pinch, prick, or torment you--bear all; only

speak not a word, and at twelve o'clock they must go away. The second

night twelve others will come: and the third night twenty-four, who

will even cut off your head; but at the twelfth hour of that night their

power is gone, and I shall be free, and will come and bring you the

Water of Life, and will wash you with it, and bring you back to life

and health.' And all came to pass as she had said; Heinel bore all, and

spoke not a word; and the third night the princess came, and fell on his

neck and kissed him. Joy and gladness burst forth throughout the castle,

the wedding was celebrated, and he was crowned king of the Golden

Mountain.

They lived together very happily, and the queen had a son. And thus

eight years had passed over their heads, when the king thought of his

father; and he began to long to see him once again. But the queen was

against his going, and said, 'I know well that misfortunes will come

upon us if you go.' However, he gave her no rest till she agreed. At his

going away she gave him a wishing-ring, and said, 'Take this ring, and

put it on your finger; whatever you wish it will bring you; only promise

never to make use of it to bring me hence to your father's house.' Then

he said he would do what she asked, and put the ring on his finger, and

wished himself near the town where his father lived.

Heinel found himself at the gates in a moment; but the guards would

not let him go in, because he was so strangely clad. So he went up to a

neighbouring hill, where a shepherd dwelt, and borrowed his old frock,

and thus passed unknown into the town. When he came to his father's

house, he said he was his son; but the merchant would not believe him,

and said he had had but one son, his poor Heinel, who he knew was long

since dead: and as he was only dressed like a poor shepherd, he would

not even give him anything to eat. The king, however, still vowed that

he was his son, and said, 'Is there no mark by which you would know me

if I am really your son?' 'Yes,' said his mother, 'our Heinel had a mark

like a raspberry on his right arm.' Then he showed them the mark, and

they knew that what he had said was true.

He next told them how he was king of the Golden Mountain, and was

married to a princess, and had a son seven years old. But the merchant

said, 'that can never be true; he must be a fine king truly who travels

about in a shepherd's frock!' At this the son was vexed; and forgetting

his word, turned his ring, and wished for his queen and son. In an

instant they stood before him; but the queen wept, and said he had

broken his word, and bad luck would follow. He did all he could to

soothe her, and she at last seemed to be appeased; but she was not so in

truth, and was only thinking how she should punish him.

One day he took her to walk with him out of the town, and showed her

the spot where the boat was set adrift upon the wide waters. Then he sat

himself down, and said, 'I am very much tired; sit by me, I will rest my

head in your lap, and sleep a while.' As soon as he had fallen asleep,

however, she drew the ring from his finger, and crept softly away, and

wished herself and her son at home in their kingdom. And when he awoke

he found himself alone, and saw that the ring was gone from his finger.

'I can never go back to my father's house,' said he; 'they would say I

am a sorcerer: I will journey forth into the world, till I come again to

my kingdom.'

So saying he set out and travelled till he came to a hill, where three

giants were sharing their father's goods; and as they saw him pass they

cried out and said, 'Little men have sharp wits; he shall part the goods

between us.' Now there was a sword that cut off an enemy's head whenever

the wearer gave the words, 'Heads off!'; a cloak that made the owner

invisible, or gave him any form he pleased; and a pair of boots that

carried the wearer wherever he wished. Heinel said they must first let

him try these wonderful things, then he might know how to set a value

upon them. Then they gave him the cloak, and he wished himself a fly,

and in a moment he was a fly. 'The cloak is very well,' said he: 'now

give me the sword.' 'No,' said they; 'not unless you undertake not to

say, "Heads off!" for if you do we are all dead men.' So they gave it

him, charging him to try it on a tree. He next asked for the boots also;

and the moment he had all three in his power, he wished himself at

the Golden Mountain; and there he was at once. So the giants were left

behind with no goods to share or quarrel about.

As Heinel came near his castle he heard the sound of merry music; and

the people around told him that his queen was about to marry another

husband. Then he threw his cloak around him, and passed through the

castle hall, and placed himself by the side of the queen, where no one

saw him. But when anything to eat was put upon her plate, he took it

away and ate it himself; and when a glass of wine was handed to her, he

took it and drank it; and thus, though they kept on giving her meat and

drink, her plate and cup were always empty.

Upon this, fear and remorse came over her, and she went into her chamber

alone, and sat there weeping; and he followed her there. 'Alas!' said

she to herself, 'was I not once set free? Why then does this enchantment

still seem to bind me?'

'False and fickle one!' said he. 'One indeed came who set thee free, and

he is now near thee again; but how have you used him? Ought he to

have had such treatment from thee?' Then he went out and sent away the

company, and said the wedding was at an end, for that he was come back

to the kingdom. But the princes, peers, and great men mocked at him.

However, he would enter into no parley with them, but only asked them

if they would go in peace or not. Then they turned upon him and tried

to seize him; but he drew his sword. 'Heads Off!' cried he; and with the

word the traitors' heads fell before him, and Heinel was once more king

of the Golden Mountain.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play and sing. They have a little house in the garden. They go there every day.

One day, they see a big dog. The dog is not nice. The dog is angry. The dog runs to the little house. Lily and Tom are scared. They try to hide.

The dog finds them. The dog barks and bites. Lily and Tom cry and scream. They want help. But no one hears them.

The dog hurts them a lot. Lily and Tom stop crying and screaming. They stop playing and singing. They are very sad. The dog is very bad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Josie. She was only three years old. Today, she was feeling a bit bored and had nothing to do.

Then, she thought of an idea. She decided to explore her attic. She was excited to see what she would find.

As she went up the stairs, the air became a bit stuffy. She opened the door to the attic, only to find it dark and dull.

Suddenly, she saw something increase in the corner. She walked closer and was surprised to find a light switch.

Josie scooted a bit closer and asked, "Oh, what do you do?"

The light switch answered, "I make the attic light up with my magic. Would you like to try it?"

Josie shouted with excitement, "Yes please!"

The light switch shined brightly, brightly illuminating the attic. Josie was amazed at how the dull attic was now full of colour and life.

Josie smiled and thanked the light switch for its work. The light switch smiled back and said, "You're welcome Josie!"

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a weak old man named Tom. Tom had a big iron, which he used to press his clothes. One day, he needed help with his iron because it was too heavy for him.

Tom went to his friend, Sam, and said, "Sam, please help me with my iron. I am too weak to use it." Sam agreed and said, "Sure, Tom. I will help you." So, Sam went to Tom's house and helped him press his clothes with the iron.

After they were done, Tom thanked Sam and said, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good friend." Sam smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tom. I am always here to help you." And from that day on, they became the best of friends and always helped each other when they needed it.

One day, a little girl named Lily went outside to play. The weather was sunny and warm. She saw her friend, Tim, sitting on the grass. He looked sad and sorry.

Lily sat down next to Tim and asked, "Why are you sad?" Tim whispered, "I lost my toy car." Lily wanted to help Tim feel better, so she said, "Let's look for it together!"

They looked under the trees, behind the bushes, and in the sandbox. Finally, they found the toy car hiding in the tall grass. Tim was so happy, he hugged Lily and said, "Thank you for helping me!" From that day on, Lily and Tim were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Bob. He was three years old and was very curious about the world around him.

One sunny day, Bob was walking in his neighbourhood. He noticed a kind lady walking towards him. He said hello and the lady said hello back. Bob thanked the lady for taking the time to say hello.

He asked the lady why she was so kind. The lady smiled and said that it was important to be kind to everyone.

Bob thought it was a very thoughtful thing to say and thanked the lady again. The lady was happy to hear that and smiled at Bob.

Bob went on his way with a smile on his face. He felt happy to have met a kind and thoughtful lady.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, Lily saw a big rhinoceros at the park. She went to her friend Tommy and said, "Look, Tommy! A big rhinoceros!" Tommy replied, "Wow! Let's go see it!"

As they got closer, the rhinoceros started to tear up the grass with its strong horn. Lily and Tommy were scared, but then they heard a voice. It was the rhinoceros talking! "Don't be afraid," said the rhinoceros. "I'm just playing. I like to tear up the grass. It's fun!"

Lily and Tommy were surprised that the rhinoceros could talk, but they were happy to make a new friend. They played with the rhinoceros for a while, tearing up the grass together. When it was time to go home, Lily and Tommy said goodbye to their new friend and went home, happy and excited about their adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a best friend named Max who lived next door. They loved to play together every day.

One day, Max decided to surprise Lily with an amazing gift. He had found a pretty flower in his garden and wanted to give it to her. When Lily saw the flower, she was so happy and gave Max a big hug.

"Thank you, Max! You are the best friend ever!" said Lily.

Max smiled and said, "I wanted to make you happy because that's what friends do. We always try to make each other happy."

Lily learned that day that being a good friend means doing nice things for each other and making each other happy. She was grateful to have such a wonderful friend like Max.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite jacket with a heavy zipper. One day, Lily was playing outside with her friends when she accidentally broke the zipper on her jacket. She tried to fix it herself, but it was too hard.

Lily's friend, Timmy, saw her struggling and asked, "What's wrong, Lily?"

"My zipper is broken and it won't close," Lily said sadly.

Timmy said, "Don't worry, I'll call my mom. She's really good at fixing things."

Soon enough, Timmy's mom arrived and fixed the zipper on Lily's jacket. Lily was so happy and thanked Timmy and his mom. From that day on, Lily knew that if something was too hard to fix, she could always call for help.

One day, two cousins, Alex and June, went to the park. Alex ran over the to the swing and jumped eagerly onto it.

"I want to play on the swing," he said to June.

June nodded and replied, "I think that sounds like fun."

The two cousins pushed each other on the swing, giggling all the while. Eventually, they got off the swing and Alex spotted something sour on the ground.

"What is that?" Alex asked June, picking it up and sniffing it delicately.

June stepped closer and said, "It's a sour apple. Taste it, see if you like it!"

Alex reached out and took a big bite. He chewed thoughtfully and then smiled.

"It tastes sweet," he said happily.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a stuffed bear named Teddy. Teddy was very special to Lily because he belonged to her mommy when she was a little girl too.

One day, Lily's mommy told her that they were going on a trip next week. Lily was excited! She loved going on trips with her mommy. But then, her mommy told her that they were going to a scary place. Lily didn't like scary places, but she trusted her mommy and knew that she would keep her safe.

The night before the trip, Lily couldn't sleep. She was too scared. But then she remembered Teddy. He always made her feel better when she was scared. She hugged him tightly and fell asleep. The next day, they went on the trip and it was indeed a little scary. But Lily had Teddy with her and she felt safe. When they came back home, Lily knew that Teddy belonged with her forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a glove that he loved very much. He wore the glove every day when he went outside to play.

One day, Tim could not find his glove. He looked under his bed and in his toy box, but it was not there. Tim felt miserable without his glove. He asked his mom, "Mom, have you seen my glove?"

Mom shook her head and said, "No, Tim. I have not seen your glove. But let's look for it together." So, they looked in the living room, the kitchen, and the yard. But they still could not find the glove.

Finally, they found the glove in the park, on the swing where Tim had played the day before. Tim was so happy to see his glove again. He said, "I missed you, glove!" From that day on, Tim made sure to keep his glove close so he would never lose it again.

Once upon a time, there was a charming frog. He lived in a pond and wanted nothing more than to follow his dream.

One night, he hopped out of the pond and went for a walk to the woods. Suddenly he saw a rainbow, bright and beautiful! He hopped closer and noticed that the rainbow had a pot of gold at the end.

The frog was so excited that he quickly hopped up to it and started to grab the gold. As he approached, a sharp voice called out from the trees.

"Wait! What are you doing?" The voice asked.

The frog looked around and saw a beautiful fairy. She was charming and friendly.

"I was trying to get the gold," said the frog.

The fairy smiled and said, "Follow your dreams - the true treasure lies within. The gold will not make you happy."

The frog thanked the fairy and hopped away. He remembered the fairy's words and kept following his dream.

Once upon a time there was a happy little girl called Daisy. She was three years old and very lively. Every morning she would request a special rhythm to start her day.

She asked her dad every day to make up a rhythm with her. He was so glad to hear her request, so he could not resist. So they would clap, tap and sing a fun and bouncy tune. Daisy would giggle and dance along, she was so full of joy.

Every day when Daisy heard the rhythm she would get so excited. She was even more glad when they took it outside, so they could share it with everyone around.

The rhythm made everyone smile, the neighbours were all delighted to hear it. Everyone was glad and happy, the rhythm gave them life.

From then on Daisy would always remember how the rhythm made her feel and she still requests it to this day.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little bunny named Floppy. Floppy liked to hop around in the grass and play with his friends. One day, Floppy's friends wanted to play a game of tag. Floppy was too shy to join in at first, but then he decided to give it a try.

As Floppy was hopping around, he noticed that his feet were starting to hurt. His shoes were too small and didn't fit him anymore. Floppy's mom took him to the store to buy new shoes. They found a pair that fit him perfectly!

With his new shoes, Floppy was able to run and play without any pain. He loved the motion of running and jumping with his friends. Floppy was no longer shy and had a great time playing with his friends.

One day, a cheerful little girl named Molly went to the park. Everywhere around her were exciting things to play with and discover.

Molly heard some clapping and went to investigate. To her delight, she found a large group of people clapping, singing, and dancing all around her.

Molly decided to join in the fun. She clapped above her head, danced around the park, and sang along to the music. Soon, everyone was singing, clapping and dancing together.

Then a carrot appeared, making its way around the circle. Everyone was so excited and clapped even louder.

Molly was so happy with the surprise that she smiled and clapped her hands again. All of a sudden, the carrot was opened up and a big bunch of colorful balloons were released in the sky.

The sky was so cheerful and beautiful with all the colorful balloons, everyone was clapping and laughing. Molly was so excited and started clapping with joy.

The cheerful day was a very special one for Molly and she was sure she never would forget it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who went to visit her grandma in the countryside. The girl was really excited to go to the countryside, because she has heard lots of stories about the beautiful flowers there. When she arrived, the little girl ran around and saw lots of different flowers in the garden of her grandma's house. She was so amazed by the beautiful flowers that she ran around slowly so that she can admire each and every one of them.

Suddenly, the little girl stopped and saw a beautiful flower that no one else seemed to notice. It was a very small flower growing slowly in the grass. The little girl slowly reached out to pluck the flower, but her grandma suddenly said: "No sweetheart, don't pick the flower. It takes a very long time for it to grow and if you pick it, it won't be able to grow anymore."

The little girl thought for a moment and then smiled. She told her grandma that if she let the flower grow, then it will be much bigger and brighter for her next visit.

Moral of the story: Sometimes it is better to appreciate something and leave it be, because it may surprise you with its beauty later on.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who found a big jewel. The jewel was very pretty and sparkled in the sun. She was so happy to find it! But then a bad man came by and took the jewel. He stole it from her and ran away.

The little girl was very upset. She knew she couldn't get her jewel back because the bad man was gone. She started to cry.

Her parents saw this and wanted to help. They went out to find the bad man and get the jewel back. After a while they found him, and they got the jewel back and gave it to the little girl.

The little girl was no longer upset. She was very happy to have the jewel back and thanked her parents for getting it back for her.

And that is the story of how the little girl got her magical jewel back. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little olive. The olive lived on a big tree with many other olives. They all wanted to become famous one day. They knew that if they were famous, people would love them and want to eat them.

One day, a nice man came to the tree. He picked the little olive and took it to his home. The man put the olive in a jar with other olives. The little olive was so happy to be with new friends. They all talked about how they wanted to become famous.

The man took the jar to a big party. At the party, people ate the olives and said, "These are the best olives ever!" The little olive was so happy to be eaten by the people. The olives in the jar became famous because everyone loved them. And the little olive was the most famous of them all.

Lily was sick. She had a bad cough and a sore throat. She did not want to play or eat. She only wanted to sleep. Her mom was worried. She gave Lily a pill to make her feel better. But Lily did not like the pill. It was big and bitter. She spit it out.

"Please, Lily, you have to take the pill," her mom said. "It will help you get well soon."

"No, no, no!" Lily cried. "I don't want the pill. It's yucky!"

Her mom tried to be patient. She hugged Lily and said, "I know, sweetie, but it's good for you. How about this? If you take the pill, I will let you watch your favorite show. The one with the lovely princess and the funny dragon. You love that show, don't you?"

Lily thought for a moment. She did love that show. It always made her laugh and smile. She wanted to see the princess and the dragon. Maybe the pill was not so bad after all. She nodded and said, "Okay, mom, I will take the pill. But only if you let me watch the show."

Her mom smiled and said, "Deal." She gave Lily a glass of water and the pill. Lily swallowed the pill quickly and made a face. Then she ran to the couch and turned on the TV. Her mom joined her and cuddled with her. They watched the show together and laughed and smiled. Lily felt a little better. She was glad she took the pill. And she was glad her mom let her watch the show. She loved her mom very much.

Mum and Dad had a surprise for Alice. They wanted to give her a letter. They found a pink envelope and they wrote something special on it. Alice was so excited to see what was inside. She jumped up and down with joy.

Dad handed her the envelope, but he said she couldn't open it yet. Alice was disappointed, but she promised to wait.

Next day, Mum and Dad took Alice to the park. They said she could open the pink envelope now. Inside, Alice found a letter. It said, 'We love you!' Alice was so happy. She smiled and hugged Mum and Dad. She knew that the letter was from them and it meant so much to her.

Alice kept the pink envelope with her letter safe forever. She was so excited every time she read it. She would never forget how wonderful that day was when she opened her pink envelope.

One morning, the sun was shining brightly when suddenly, it started to rain. Soon, big drops of water were falling fast and it was raining harder and harder.

Jojo and his mom were sad because they couldn't go outside and play. But then, Jojo had an idea - he said, "Mom, let's make dough!" So the two of them went into the kitchen and mixed together flour and water to make some dough.

Once the dough was ready, Jojo and his mom had lots of fun making shapes and figures with it. They rolled it into little snakes and made round doughnuts and cut out canoes. After a while, the rain had stopped and outside the sun was shining again. Jojo and his mom were happy, for now they could go outside and play!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys. One day, he found a big cube in his toy box. It was red and shiny. He picked it up and it was heavy. Timmy wondered how much it weighed.

Later that day, Timmy's mom made him a sandwich for lunch. But when he took a bite, he made a face. The sandwich tasted bad! Timmy didn't like it at all.

After lunch, Timmy went back to playing with his toys. He decided to weigh the cube with his toy scale. It was very heavy! Timmy was surprised. He played with the cube for a while longer, but then he got bored. He put it back in his toy box and went to play outside.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky was very excited because today was his birthday. He waddled around the pond, quacking happily.

Suddenly, Ducky saw his friend, Bunny. Bunny said, "Happy birthday, Ducky! I have a surprise for you." Bunny spread his arms and revealed a big carrot cake.

Ducky was so excited that he flapped his wings and splashed water everywhere. "Thank you, Bunny! Let's share the cake with all our friends," Ducky said. So, they invited all the animals in the pond to the party and everyone had a great time eating cake and swimming.

Lily and Ben were playing with their bikes in the park. They liked to ride fast and make turns and jumps. Lily was good at balancing on one wheel. She could lift her front wheel or her back wheel and keep going. Ben wanted to learn how to do that too.

"Can you teach me how to balance on one wheel?" Ben asked Lily.

"Sure, I can teach you. It is fun and easy. You just have to pedal hard and lean a little bit," Lily said. She was generous and liked to help her friend.

Lily showed Ben how to balance on one wheel. She lifted her front wheel and rode for a few seconds. Then she lifted her back wheel and rode for a few more seconds. She smiled and waved at Ben.

"Wow, you are so good at balancing on one wheel. Let me try," Ben said. He tried to copy Lily, but he was not very good. He lifted his front wheel, but he lost his balance and fell down. He scraped his knee and started to cry.

"Ouch, that hurts. I can't balance on one wheel. It is too hard," Ben said.

Lily got off her bike and ran to Ben. She hugged him and said, "Don't cry, Ben. It is okay. You just need to practice more. You can do it. I will help you. Here, take my band-aid and put it on your knee. It will make you feel better."

Lily gave Ben her band-aid. She was generous and kind. Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. Can we try again?"

"Of course, we can try again. Come on, let's get back on our bikes and have some fun," Lily said.

Lily and Ben got back on their bikes and tried to balance on one wheel. They had some falls and some laughs, but they did not give up. They had fun and learned something new. They were happy and proud.

Once there was a pupil who was very creative. He liked to use his imagination to come up with different ideas. One day, he had a great idea. He decided he was going to try and win a special competition - a race!

He practised and practised with all his might, so that he could become faster. On the day of the competition, he was ready to win! He made sure that he had his running shoes and a bottle of water.

The race started, and the pupil sprinted forward. He ran as fast as he could, and finally, he crossed the finish line first. He had won the race! Everyone cheered and congratulated the pupil on his victory.

He was so proud of himself. He knew that all his hard work, practice and creativity had paid off. He had won the race and achieved something special, and it made him very happy.

Once upon a time there was an orange needle called Frank. He had been in the same spot for years and he was getting bored. He wanted to explore, but he didn't know how to.

Then one day, a small 3 year old child saw Frank. The child said "Hello Frank! I'm going to help you explore the world." Frank was so excited!

The child said, "I think we should reverse!" Frank looked confused, but the child explained that it meant going backwards, the opposite of forwards.

So, the child and Frank started reversing. They went up and down, side to side and around in circles. Frank was enjoying his adventure!

After an hour of reversing, the child and Frank stopped. The child said, "Wow, that was a lot of fun! You now know that you can explore by reversing."

Frank thanked the child for his help and then said goodbye. As the child walked away, Frank knew that he would never forget this adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Margaret. Margaret wanted to go to the park to play, but her mother said she had to stay home. Margaret was sad, so she looked for something to do.

Suddenly, Margaret saw a trap on the ground. It looked like a box with a hole in the top. Margaret didn't know what the trap was.

"Mommy," she asked. "What is this?"

"It's a harmless animal trap," explained her mom. "It's a way to introduce animals we can study and learn about."

That sounded exciting! Margaret decided to try her own animal trap. She got a box and placed it outside, putting some food inside.

Sure enough, an animal came to the trap looking for food. Margaret was so excited! She looked closely and saw that it was a cute little mouse.

Margaret felt happy. She had introduced something new to the world â€" and it was harmless!
